subject: Clarification on hybrid-model charge allocation and rounding for MedicSoft
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena.park@medicsoft.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@medicsoft.com
Date: Sat, 30 Jun 2028 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Question on how hybrid pipeline usage shows up on invoice

Hi Kimberly —

Thanks for taking a look at this — we pulled our Q2 invoice and noticed a couple of lines that look inconsistent with what we expected, and I wanted to confirm the billing mechanics so we can reconcile on our side before finance closes the quarter. Attaching a redacted invoice sample (MedicSoft_Q2_invoice_sample.pdf).

Two specific items:
1) Our product uses a hybrid pipeline where most user sessions start on the 8k model and only occasionally escalate to the 32k model for long-context searches. The invoice shows separate token charges under both models for the same session IDs — is that expected or should those be rolled up?

2) The invoice appears to apply a per-invocation rounding/minimum for very small calls (under ~200 tokens) that inflates the apparent token count. Can you confirm the rounding quantum and whether those small calls are aggregated for billing?

We also have a tiered discount in our SOW and want to understand how blended rates are computed when a single user session touches multiple model SKUs. If you can outline the attribution rules and any proration logic, that would help.

If easier, we can jump on a short call — procurement would like a written summary for our AP team.

Thanks —
Elena Park
Director, Procurement
MedicSoft

Attachment: MedicSoft_Q2_invoice_sample.pdf
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@medicsoft.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 30 Jun 2028 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question on how hybrid pipeline usage shows up on invoice

Hi Elena —

Appreciate the note and the sample invoice, good catch. Short answer up front: hybrid pipelines are not double-billed for the same token: we attribute each token to the model that actually produced it, but there are several layers (per-invocation minimums, per-request model-class mapping, and the discount-blending rule) that together create the lines you see. Below is a concise breakdown and an example mapping that should make reconciliation straightforward.

1) Per-invocation attribution
- Every request is evaluated by the router and assigned to a model variant at the time of generation. Tokens produced are billed at that model variant's per-token rate. If a session invokes model A (8k) then later model B (32k), the tokens are billed to the specific invocations respectively — not duplicated.

2) Aggregation and rounding
- Small invocations (<= 256 tokens) are grouped into a 1K 'micro-batch' window for invoice presentation by default, which can make line items look inflated. We do this to reduce noise and accounting overhead for extremely small calls.
- For customers who prefer finer-grained tokenization on the invoice, we can switch you to the 'detail' invoice profile (no 1K micro-batch window) — caveat: this increases line-item counts and may expose more variance month-to-month.

3) Discount blending for hybrid sessions
- Blended rates are computed at the invoice-line level by mapping each model SKU to its effective rate and then applying your contracted tier discounts to the aggregate token spend per SKU. There is no additional per-session reweighting. So if 90% of tokens are on the 8k SKU and 10% on 32k, the blended effective rate follows that split.

4) Session amortization and minimums
- Reserved / commit credits and session minimums are amortized across the calendar month. For trueups or pilot concessions we can apply a per-deal carve that caps rounding at 256 tokens for the pilot quarter.

Example (from your invoice): a session with 3 small 80-token calls on 8k and one 1,200-token escalation to 32k will show:
- 8k model: 3 * 80 tokens aggregated into a 1K micro-batch line (unless you request detail-profile)
- 32k model: 1,200 tokens billed at 32k per-token rate

I've attached a short walkthrough (redwood_billing_walkthrough.xlsx) with a worked example using your invoice numbers and the formulas so you can drop it into your AP reconciliation.

If you want, Jordan is copied here to propose a temporary concession that reduces the micro-batch minimum for the pilot. Ben/Karthik — tagging you for pricing confirmation before I send a formal note.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Customer Billing
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_billing_walkthrough.xlsx
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 30 Jun 2028 13:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question on how hybrid pipeline usage shows up on invoice

Kimberly / team —

Thanks for the clear breakdown. From a go-forward commercial perspective I propose the following one-quarter pilot concession for MedicSoft (deal MED-2028-Q3) to help close the reconciliation gap:

- Apply a capped micro-batch floor of 256 tokens (instead of the default 1K) for December-January-February billing cycles for this account only.
- For hybrid sessions where tokens cross SKUs in the same session, compute a blended effective rate but guarantee that the blended floor cannot exceed the higher-SKU per-invocation minimum (i.e., protects Redwood's tail-costs).
- No change to long-term pricing or to your tier ladder; this is a temporary invoice presentation and rounding concession to speed AP reconciliation.

If Ben and Karthik are good, I'll approve in HubSpot and we can send a short amendment (proposed_concession_term.docx) for Elena to sign. This keeps legal exposure minimal but gives them the documentation AP wants.

Ben — any objections on the floor/cap numbers? Karthik — do we need an engineer ticket to flip their invoice profile for detail vs summary?

—Jordan
VP, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Thank you, that explanation is very helpful. The worked example in your walkthrough lined up with our internal counts. MedicSoft is happy to accept the proposed one-quarter pilot concession (256-token floor) and the blended-rate confirmation for hybrid sessions, subject to a short amendment we can share with our legal / AP.

Please send the amendment and confirm the change to the invoice profile (we prefer summary view for now but would like the option to switch to detail if reconciliation becomes noisy). Once we have the amended SOW (MED-2028-Q3 amendment) we'll sign and loop in AP.
